column1: # Player-facing settings: the iOS launcher (dm/ios/Sources/Launcher.swift) and the Mac app's settings window (dm/mac/Launcher.swift) show them before the game starts; Mac front ends read the same list.

# dm/games/settings.py writes one game's list into its app (dm/launcher.json; build_ipa.sh, and dm/mac/pack_app.py through the NSP script): the rows whose condition holds for that game, with its defaults. Each sets an environment variable the host reads when the game starts; one an env file sets
# (Documents/env.txt, the bundle's dm/env.txt) is shown but kept. Diagnostic switches stay environment-only, so they are not listed here. The player's page is docs/settings.md.
#   variable  the environment variable the setting sets

#   kind      choice: values value=label,..., an option only some games have with ?<shown>&<shown> after its label (languages: the game's own, from its control data; every language when it has none, with a note); range: values low:high:step, shown as a percentage;
#             toggle: values - (on sets 1, off 0) or <on>/<off>, the two values the variable takes (on/off)
#   default   a value (a toggle's: 1 on, 0 off); DM_GAME_<NAME>: the host's own default from the game profile (game_profile.h, game.py); build:<VAR>: the IPA build's setting (build_ipa.sh)
#             <ios>|<mac> selects the platform's default before resolving a profile macro or build variable
#   shown     Conditions may be joined with &. runtime:DM_VARIABLE=value requires a complete runtime manifest matching the rewritten module (Mac only).

#             always; DM_GAME_<NAME>!=<value> or ==<value>; fixups:<KEY>: main's rewriter table has that key (a stub in the game's build, patch_nso.py); languages>1 (more than one to pick, so also when the control data lists none); gfxapi:<API>: the packer's GFXAPI;
#             platform:<ios | mac>: the app's platform (SETTINGS_PLATFORM, ios when unset), for a switch only that platform's front end reads
#   section   Game, Controls or Performance: a heading on the single settings screen. Rows appear in table order within each section
#             Reset to tested defaults clears all launcher choices; values fixed by an env file stay
#   label, note  the setting's name and the line under it (may be empty; only for a setting with a cost: latency, memory, heat)
#   meta      optional, key=value pairs separated by ; (settings.py META lists the keys; docs/frontends.md, The settings list, describes them):
#             level=basic  a setting a front end shows first;  needs=<VAR>=<value>  a sub-setting, drawn only while the row that sets <VAR> has that value

column8: Sets resolution, anti-aliasing, texture sharpness, output scaling, shadows, occlusion, bounce light, contact shadows, reflections, fog, model quality and draw distance together; the frame rate, screen ratio, dynamic resolution, anisotropy and memory settings stay as you chose them (Performance also sets 120 fps). Custom shows every one of those settings. Maximum needs about 5 GB of GPU memory and runs near 40 fps on an M4 Max. Restart required.
Fixed modes render the scene and output at the selected size. Higher resolutions need Extended game memory. Later combat and movies still need testing.

Draws the menus, HUD text and icons at the render resolution instead of 1280x720 stretched to it: sharp edges at 1440p, 4K and 5K. Works with a fixed render resolution above; the minimap keeps its own size. Restart required.
16:10 keeps the horizontal view and shows more above and below. Adjusts perspective and flat UI cameras, world markers and HUD anchors. Movies retain 16:9. Restart required.
High detects finer edges and searches twice as far. Higher render resolutions also reduce jagged edges. Fine texture detail may still shimmer.

Prefers finer existing texture mipmaps on surfaces. Combine with 16x anisotropic filtering. Very sharp can shimmer in motion; this does not replace textures with higher-resolution assets. Restart required.

column3: off=Original (bilinear),scale=Clean scaling,lanczos=Lanczos scaling,sharp_low=Clean + light sharpening,sharp=Clean + sharpening,sharp_high=Clean + strong sharpening
column8: How the finished picture is scaled to your screen and, optionally, sharpened (contrast adaptive, no halos around text). Clean scaling uses a bicubic filter when the picture is shown at its size or larger and a box filter over each pixel's footprint when it is shown smaller, for example a 5K picture in a smaller window. Every mode except Original also dithers the output, which hides the banding of dark gradients. Applies to the whole picture including the interface. Restart required.
Each atlas contains four tiles. High gives each tile 2048 pixels; Ultra gives 4096 pixels. Adds 48 or 240 MB of shadow storage and increases GPU work.

Scales the distances at which the sun's four shadow cascades change (11, 30, 150 and 200 m in the first stage), so shadows reach farther before they fade, and every cascade covers a larger area with the same atlas: shadows near you become softer by the same factor unless Shadows: Resolution is Ultra. Costs nothing by itself. Restart required.

Replaces the sun shadow's filter: a blocker search finds how far the caster is, and the edge softens with that distance (sharp where an object touches the ground, softer farther from it) through a disc of bilinear compares. Costs GPU time in shadowed areas. Restart required.

Short screen-space rays from each surface toward the sun add small shadows where objects touch the ground or each other, which the shadow maps are too coarse to hold. The sun direction is read from the game's own shadow cascades. Uses the occlusion pass (selecting it with Ambient occlusion Off runs that pass at Low). Increases GPU work. Restart required.

Adds depth-based contact shading before transparencies and the interface. Higher levels sample more directions; all use half-resolution shading with a depth-aware filter. Increases GPU work. Restart required.

Adds coloured light bounced from nearby lit surfaces into occluded corners, using the occlusion pass (selecting it with Ambient occlusion Off runs that pass at Low). Only surfaces visible on screen can bounce light; fires and bright signs tint their surroundings. Increases GPU work. Restart required.

Traces the lit picture on horizontal surfaces (roads, floors) seen at a grazing angle, where wet or rough asphalt shows a sheen of the lights and fires in front of it. Only what is on screen can reflect, and the game gives no material information, so it is limited to grazing angles and kept soft; the game's own reflection probes stay. Uses the occlusion pass (runs it at Low when Ambient occlusion is Off). Increases GPU work. Restart required.

Changes the native distance fog on surfaces. Original preserves the art direction; Dense adds atmosphere rather than detail. Particles and scripted fog effects retain their own settings. Restart required.
High and Very high reduce detail thresholds by 2 and 4. Maximum retains the most detailed model at every visible distance. Does not add polygons or spawn extra characters. Restart required.
Maximum disables the model disappearance threshold. Frustum culling and the game's object spawning remain active. More CPU and GPU work; restart required.
Extended reserves more address space for high-resolution render targets. Only memory the game uses takes RAM.
Full-output modes are experimental. Start with 1080p; check scanning and cutscenes. 1800p retains the confirmed rendering path.
With Native, 1080p, 2K, 4K or 5K: fills a 16:10 screen while keeping proportions. Crops 5% from each side. Automatically fits the HUD and pause menus.
Extended lets 5K, Ultra shadows, Maximum model detail and High fog fit together; Switch-sized memory can run out when a new area loads. Only what the game touches takes RAM.

Lets the native controller lower scene resolution under load. Off holds the selected maximum. Astral Chain offers 100/90/80% scene sizes; its Original automatic mode keeps console behavior. MP4 reference modes keep their original behavior.
Sharper ground and walls seen at an angle. 16x costs little on a Mac.
Sharper shadow edges. High uses 24 MB more GPU memory; Ultra 120 MB and more GPU time.
Keeps objects detailed further away. Far and Very far move the switch to simpler models 2 or 4 times further out; Maximum always draws the most detailed model. More GPU time.
Fog and light shafts at full resolution: cleaner edges around objects. Uses more GPU time and 100 MB or more GPU memory at 1800p.
Uses more GPU time and can increase heat.
Fill crops the game's 16:9 picture to cover the screen. Health bars, subtitles or maps near the edges can be cut off. A full-screen picture without cropping needs a patch for each game.
Plays Joy-Con 2 and Pro Controller 2 over Bluetooth: hold Sync on one during the game to pair it. macOS asks once for Bluetooth access.
Renders about a quarter more pixels: a little slower and warmer.
Softens loud moments instead of clipping them: fewer crackles in loud fights.
Up to one frame more display latency.
Keeps a pipeline archive; uses more memory.
The first start waits a few minutes for it, once.
